newsitem.title: UK: Motorcycling-Doohan set to join Hailwood, Agostini.
newsitem.headline: Motorcycling-Doohan set to join Hailwood, Agostini.

text.p: Michael Doohan could watch the last five races of the 500cc grand prix season from the stands and still lift the world title. His advantage is that supreme.
The Australian, first nine times and second once in 10 starts, needs only a top seven finish in the British Grand Prix at Donington Park on Sunday to clinch his fourth successive title.
For either of his main rivals -- Japan's Tadayuki Okada or Nobuatsu Aoki -- to have a chance, Doohan must fail to finish in every race and one of them must win them all five.
Doohan currently has 245 points. Okada, his Honda team mate who has had injury problems and has never raced a 500 at Donington, 129. Aoki, his left shoulder blade broken in Brazil recently, 126.
Doohan is about to become only the third rider to claim four championships in a row, putting him alongside bike racing greats Mike Hailwood and Giacomo Agostini.
He will be only the sixth rider to win four 500cc titles and a victory at Donington would also equal Agostini's record of 10 wins in one season.
"Now I enjoy what I am doing. I have achieved, in terms of world titles, what I wanted. Now I am racing because I enjoy it," said a relaxed Doohan in the run-up to the race.
Doohan has won on Donington's twisty but fast circuit for the last two years so will be feeling confident that he can complete the hat-trick.
Spaniard Alex Criville, the only man to have beaten Doohan this season, has been out since suffering severe hand injuries in practice for the Dutch Grand Prix in June.
His team had raised the possibility of him racing at Donington but that return has now been delayed until at least the Czech Grand Prix on August 31.
In the 250cc category, Italy's Max Biaggi will be hoping to ride his Honda back into the championship lead. Like Doohan, he will also be looking for a hat-trick of chequered flags at Donington.
His fifth place at the Brazilian Grand Prix earlier this month meant he slipped into second place in the championship behind Japan's Tetsuya Harada.
Ralf Waldman of Germany is breathing down both their necks with only nine points fewer than Biaggi.
The 125cc category, like the 500cc, has also become a one man show, with Italy's Valentino Rossi having won eight races to build up a 77-point lead.
